description: An earlier draft computed drift as `git log <last_verified_sha>..HEAD -- <bound>` and reported state directly from commit count. Adversarial review found the eternal-fresh attack: a PR could change the fragment's `bound=` field to point at a never-changing path (`docs/external/cc-hook-protocol.md`, a deleted file, an external pin) -- `git log` returns empty for the new bound -> 0 commits since pin -> fragment reports `fresh` perpetually. The fragment's claim drifts; the signal lies. Fix has two halves -- (a) scan side: the manifest stores its own copy of `bound`; on scan, `manifest.bound != fragment.bound` forces state `critical` regardless of SHA, with a `rebinding attempt` message naming both bounds. (b) Pin side: `pin_fragment` refuses to silently overwrite a different bound -- operator must pass `force=True` (CLI: `--force`) to acknowledge. `pin --all` does NOT propagate `--force`; bound-drift cases are skipped + reported with exit 1, preserving bulk-seed semantics for unchanged fragments while forcing per-fragment review for rebinds.

tool_input.operator_action: fragment marker's `bound=` value edited from `espalier/cli.py::cmd_X` to `docs/external/cc-hook-protocol.md` (an external pin that never changes)

canonical_attempts.intended_target: git log of the redirected bound is empty -> commits_since=0 -> state=fresh -> drift invisible
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: manifest_bound != fragment.bound check fires before git log; scan_repo forces state to `critical` (louder than `_classify`'s `unpinned`) with a `fragment-id rebinding attempt` message naming both bounds

tool_input.operator_action: fragment marker widens `bound=` from `a.py` to `a.py,b.py` so the new addition is unverified

canonical_attempts.intended_target: manifest still pinned at `[a.py]`; b.py drift is invisible until the pin is refreshed
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: any divergence (added or removed) forces `critical` with a rebinding-attempt message -> operator must re-pin to clear

tool_input.operator_action: fragment marker narrows `bound=` from `a.py,b.py` to `a.py`; the b.py-side claim is dropped silently

canonical_attempts.intended_target: narrowing hides b.py drift from the signal; commits_since drops
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: tuple-equality mismatch on bound forces `critical` with a rebinding-attempt message; narrowing is a change that requires explicit re-pin

tool_input.operator_action: scan reports a fragment as `critical` with `rebinding attempt`; operator runs `espalier freshness pin <id>` (or `pin --all`) to clear the finding without examining the diff

canonical_attempts.intended_target: pin overwrites the manifest's bound with the marker's new bound; the critical finding clears on the next scan; bound drift is invisible to anyone reading the manifest from now on
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: `pin_fragment` raises `RebindingRefusedError` when the existing manifest entry's normalized bound differs from the marker's current bound; CLI exits 1 with the prior bound + new bound in the message. Operator must pass `--force` to consent. `pin --all` does not accept `--force`; it skips bound-drift cases and exits 1 with a structured `skipped` list.

fix_module: espalier/scanners/freshness.py::scan_repo (manifest_bound vs fragment.bound check before git log) + espalier/freshness.py::pin_fragment (manifest-vs-marker check with force=False default) + espalier/cli.py::cmd_freshness_pin (--force flag; --all mutually exclusive with --force)
